description: This case covers a probabilistic digital twin of operational en route airspace built for the London Area Control Centre and described in a January 2026 arXiv paper by Nick Pepper and 13 co-authors. The twin combines historical and live operational data with a probabilistic, physics-informed machine learning model of aircraft performance to reproduce real traffic scenarios while reflecting the uncertainty inherent in air traffic control. It gives a single environment for developing and testing AI agents for air traffic control, with fast-time execution up to 200 times real time, a standard Python gym interface, quantitative performance metrics and a human-machine interface through which qualified air traffic control officers assess agents. A structured assurance case following the Trustworthy and Ethical Assurance framework provides evidence of the twin's accuracy and fidelity. Coverage is UK en route airspace controlled from London. The paper is free to read on arXiv; the twin and its data are not released with it. Outcome: the authors report the first probabilistic digital twin of operational en route airspace with assurance evidence. Limitations: results are self-reported and the environment is not public. The case is related to the Simmod PRO airport model and the Cologne/Bonn airport digital twin case.
